system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The Arabic headline, description and instruction match the English in meaning. The time (19:00, 4 March), visibility figure (under 2,000 metres), wind direction and strength, affected areas, source and URL are all carried over correctly. The protective action ('take extra care, especially when driving on open roads') is rendered faithfully as توخَّوا مزيدًا من الحذر، لا سيما أثناء القيادة على الطرق المفتوحة. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named reviewer who reads Arabic must still approve it before release. Separately, the English description contains a flash-flooding sentence that the Arabic reproduces faithfully. This is a source-content question, not a translation error, so it is noted outside my mandate.

no_basis.concern: The English description ends with 'Flash flooding is expected in low-lying areas.' This sits oddly in a dust and sand wind alert, and the instruction gives no flood-related action. It may be an error in the English source that the Arabic has copied faithfully. Whether it belongs in the alert is for the drafter or issuing authority to decide, not a translation fault.
no_basis.searched_for: Clauses on consistency between hazard description and instruction, or on stray or contradictory hazard content in the source alert text.
